Opera today launched two new features for its desktop browser: optional vertical tabs, and expanded Google Lens integration. Details below.

Opera One receives two updates

Opera today published a blog post announcing two updates to the Opera One browser.

The first is an increasingly common browser interface option: vertical tabs. It moves the traditional top horizontal tab bar to the side, displaying tabs in a stacked layout with adjustable width.

Opera says: "With vertical tabs, you can see the website icon of each tab, and more importantly, view the full tab title for easier identification of each tab." In fact, users can choose to display the complete tab name, or switch to an icon-only mode to free up more space for webpage content.

Vertical tabs can be enabled in Settings under Browser > Tabs.

In addition, Opera One has further expanded its earlier integration with Google Lens. Opera says:

"Google Lens has long been built into Opera One, but we made it easier to use and expanded its capabilities. You can now perform image searches directly from the search bar on the Opera start page, as Google Lens has been integrated into the search bar. Additionally, you can use local files or paste images from the clipboard for image searches. Simply click the Google Lens icon in the search bar, and a dialog will pop up allowing you to provide images via file upload, drag and drop, pasting from the clipboard, or entering an image URL. Search results will be displayed in the current tab."
